title: Implications of Current Litigation on the Design of AI Systems for Healthcare Delivery

bias_targets.methodology: Thematic analysis of AI-related litigation and reported harms from legal and incident databases (e.g., tracking cases like the UnitedHealth follow-up algorithm, Google Derm Assist, and the VA suicide prevention tool for demonstrating racial disparities).

Thematic analysis of legal cases and reported harms involving AI systems that systematically deny, delay, or prematurely terminate healthcare coverage specifically targeting elderly patients (e.g., Medicare Advantage algorithms like nH Predict).

Thematic analysis of AI-related litigation involving algorithms that unlawfully reduce, cut, or deny medically necessary care, benefits, and support for vulnerable populations with physical disabilities or mental health challenges.

Thematic analysis of reported AI harms and litigation where algorithms negatively impacted low-income individuals or demonstrated economic bias (e.g., automated state Medicaid denial systems and the ENA Emergency Severity Index).

Thematic analysis of reported AI harms in healthcare, such as identifying algorithms (e.g., the VA suicide prevention tool) that disproportionately prioritize men while overlooking female populations.
